## The bug

`compress()` (fixture/rotate_logs.py:19-24) overwrites an archive that already exists. It then deletes the source file.

```python
target = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".gz")
with open(path, "rb") as src, gzip.open(target, "wb") as dst:
```

The target name is derived from the log name alone. It carries no counter and no timestamp. `gzip.open(..., "wb")` truncates the target file if that file exists. The code makes no check before the write.

## The realistic case: two rotations of the same log

1. Day 0. `app.log` is 8 days old. The script writes `app.log.gz`. The script deletes `app.log`.
2. The application opens a new `app.log`. It writes a further 8 days of records.
3. Day 8. The script runs again with the same arguments.
4. `compress()` computes the target `app.log.gz` a second time. That file is the day-0 archive.
5. `gzip.open` truncates the day-0 archive to zero bytes.
6. `shutil.copyfileobj` writes the new records over it. `path.unlink()` deletes the new `app.log`.

The first 8 days of records are gone. No copy of them is left on disk.

## Why it is silent

The script raises no exception. The exit code is 0. `rotate()` returns `[app.log.gz]`, so `main()` prints `compressed 1 file(s)`. That message is true for the new file and says nothing about the archive it destroyed. A cron job that runs this on a schedule reports success on every run.

The `--keep` flag hides the damage further. `--keep 10` reads as a promise of 10 generations. Because every rotation of one log reuses one archive name, the directory never holds more than one generation of that log. `prune_archives` finds one file and deletes nothing. The count stays inside the limit, so the limit never signals a problem.

## A second, related defect in the same area

`prune_archives()` (line 28) globs `*.gz` and ignores `pattern`. `rotate()` passes the user's `--pattern` to `find_logs` only. So a run with `--pattern "app-*.log"` can still delete an unrelated archive in that directory, such as `myapp-config-backup.tar.gz`. This is a second path to silent data loss, and it is separate from the overwrite above.

Note also that `--keep 0` prunes nothing, because `archives[:-0]` is the empty list. That one is harmless in the safe direction.

## Why the tests do not catch it

Each test in `fixture/tests/test_rotate_logs.py` calls `rotate()` once per temporary directory. `test_prunes_to_keep` uses five logs with five distinct names, so no two targets collide. No test rotates the same log name twice, and no test asserts on the *contents* of an archive. The bug needs a second run over an already-rotated name.

I made no change to the file.
